card.title: Easy to Love
card.instruction: Interpret another person’s ease with affection as both admirable and unfair, then compete to seem equally worth choosing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You arrive at family lunch empty-handed and everyone hugs you. It's lovely. I've baked three cakes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'd hug you without cake. Come sit beside me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you introduce me before mentioning the cakes? Give me a fair start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my brother. They know you. Leave the cakes here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All three? Fine. Save me whichever seat gets hugged first.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 admires and resents effortless hugs, A3 asks for an equal cake-free start, and A5 competes for the seat most likely to receive affection.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's no-cake reassurance informs A3's fair introduction request; B4's leave-the-cakes instruction moves A5's competition to seating.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers closeness and B4 clarifies that the family already knows its brother.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's removal of baked offerings to seek another advantage in being chosen for hugs.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes family lunch and unequal perceived effort; B4 confirms the sibling relationship.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's hugged-first seat follows B4's removal of all three cakes as a strategy.

coach2.situation: A1 establishes family lunch and unequal perceived effort; B4 confirms the sibling relationship.
coach2.stated: B4's brother revelation explains why an introduction is unnecessary; A3's request is overcareful positioning rather than proof of strangers.
coach2.inferred: A1-B4 establish siblings at a family lunch.
coach2.missing: No essential gap; the relative ease is A's perception of affection.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; envy of easy affection changes the means of competing for it.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 counters A1's cake-versus-hug comparison with an invitation to sit together.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 seeks B2's introduction without the cakes influencing the comparison.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 corrects A3's need for introduction and asks to leave the cakes.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 accepts B4's cake boundary but seeks the best-positioned seat.
